title: The Only Question
text: Someone who buys for a living looked at {company} today and asked the only question that matters: what are you?

reskins.FOOD: A food writer eats, pays cash, and asks you straight: crowd-pleaser or destination? A menu that tracks what the street sells and competes on price and speed — or one thing nobody else makes, that people cross town for.
reskins.ECOM: A veteran buyer scrolls your storefront twice and asks: everything store or the one thing? Stock what's trending and race on price and shipping — or own a niche so hard the niche means you.
reskins.TECH: An analyst sits through the demo and asks the roadmap question: feature parity or opinionated product? Match the market leader's checklist — or refuse features on purpose, because the product has a point of view.
reskins.CONTENT: A talent manager watches your last ten uploads and asks: trend-surfer or format-owner? Ride what the algorithm rewards this month — or invent a format people name after you.
reskins.FASHION: A boutique buyer flips through the rack and asks: on-trend or house style? Read the season, ship it fast, price it under — or a recognisable look that ignores the season.
reskins.GAMING: A publisher scout plays twenty minutes and asks: genre-plus or genre-defining? The proven genre with one twist, shipped fast — or the weird one that becomes its own genre or dies.
reskins.FITNESS: A member who has tried every gym in town asks at the front desk: full-service gym or the method? Every class everyone else has — or a named method that exists only here.
reskins.BEAUTY: A stockist smells the tester and asks: dupe culture or original formulation? The $12 version of the $60 product — or the formulation others dupe.
reskins.EDTECH: A district administrator reads your outcomes page and asks: curriculum coverage or outcomes brand? Teach everything the syllabus lists — or be famous for one outcome, provably.
reskins.SUSTAIN: A certifier tours the line and asks: green option or the standard-setter? The sustainable version of the normal thing — or redefine what the category must be.
reskins.TOYS: A retail buyer at the fair asks across the table: licensed safety or original IP? Ride licensed characters — or build IP worth licensing out.
reskins.PET: A rep who sells into every clinic in the county asks: shelf brand or vet brand? Win the retail shelf on price and packaging — or win the vet's recommendation and never discount.

choices.label: Track what works. Do it cheaper and faster.

outcome.narration: You said it without flinching. Proven demand, tighter execution — the follower who arrives first.

choices.label: Don't answer yet. Keep every option open.

outcome.narration: No bet placed. Sensible today. The market will keep asking.

choices.label: Name the one thing only you do.

outcome.narration: Now it's a promise, and everything you ship either keeps it or breaks it.

title: The Rival Answers First
text: {rival} planted a flag this week, loudly. The market will file {company} somewhere next to it — pick the drawer or it gets picked for you.

reskins.FOOD: {rival} opened two blocks over selling exactly what already sells. Your regulars are asking what you are now: crowd-pleaser or destination?
reskins.ECOM: {rival} just expanded into every category you touch. The question lands in your inbox: everything store or the one thing?
reskins.TECH: {rival} shipped the checklist — every feature the market leader has. So which is {company}: feature parity or opinionated product?
reskins.CONTENT: {rival} posts daily and rides every trend that moves. The comments compare you now: trend-surfer or format-owner?
reskins.FASHION: {rival} shipped the season three weeks early and priced it under everyone. So which are you: on-trend or house style?
reskins.GAMING: {rival} announced the safe version of your genre with a bigger budget. So which is this: genre-plus or genre-defining?
reskins.FITNESS: {rival} opened a bigger floor with every class in town on the schedule. The question walks in with the new members: full-service gym or the method?
reskins.BEAUTY: {rival} launched the cheap version of the category hero and it's selling. So which side are you on: dupe culture or original formulation?
reskins.EDTECH: {rival} now covers the whole syllabus and says so everywhere. So which is {company}: curriculum coverage or outcomes brand?
reskins.SUSTAIN: {rival} put a green label on the normal thing and shelved it everywhere. So which are you: green option or the standard-setter?
reskins.TOYS: {rival} signed a license every parent recognises. So which is {company}: licensed safety or original IP?
reskins.PET: {rival} bought the end-cap in every store that stocks you. So which are you: shelf brand or vet brand?

outcome.narration: You said it without flinching. Proven demand, tighter execution — the follower who arrives first.

title: Copy It
text: Everyone has seen {rival}'s new thing — your customers, your team, the group chat. Now they are all watching you to see what it means.

choices.label: Copy it fast. Your version ships in a quarter.

outcome.narration: It sells on arrival — proven demand does that. It also ages fast, and everyone knows whose idea it was.
It sells. It also gets noticed.

choices.label: Copy it better. Three quarters, out-execute it.

outcome.narration: Slower and dearer — and when it lands, nobody calls it a copy. They call it the good one.
You paid for excellence and shipped an imitation. The market can tell, even when you can't.

choices.label: Counter it. Launch your own bet against it.

outcome.narration: Your bet lands. Now there are two answers on the market, and one of them is yours alone.
Unproven demand proves itself the hard way. The team watches you eat it.

choices.label: Ignore it. Your lane is your lane.

outcome.narration: You don't blink. The people who chose you notice that you didn't.
The hit was real. A slice of the market went to find out, and some of it is not coming back.

title: They Noticed
text: {rival} posted your version next to the original. Side by side, no caption. It didn't need one.

choices.label: Say nothing. Ship the next thing.

outcome.narration: Your people shrug. They know what you are, even on a bad week.
The screenshot travels further than your product did.

choices.label: Answer it on camera.

pass.narration: You own it with a straight face, and the story becomes how you handled it.

fail.narration: You blink on camera. Now there are two clips.

title: The Comparison
text: A trade writer put {topItem} and {rival}'s answer in the same review. The winner is in the headline.

choices.label: Let the work speak.

outcome.narration: You win on the merits, in print. Clip it.
Second place, with your name spelled right.

choices.label: Work the writer before it prints.

outcome.narration: The framing lands your way. Nobody asks how.
The writer prints the phone call too.

title: The Walk-Back
text: Word got around that {company} changed its answer. Longtime customers want to know which version they signed up for. New ones want to know which version is true.

choices.label: Say it once, everywhere, loudly.

outcome.narration: One statement, no hedge. The ones who leave were already gone.

choices.label: Let the product make the argument.

outcome.narration: Quieter and cheaper. For a while nobody is sure what you are — including two people on payroll.

choices.label: Discount the old crowd into staying.

outcome.narration: They stay for the price. That is not the same as staying for you.

title: Outflanked Twice
text: The cheap one undercut you this quarter. The special one raised prices and got away with it. {company} sits in the middle, and the middle is where margins go to be split.

choices.label: Pick the lane: cheaper, faster, everywhere.

outcome.narration: Late, but a bet is finally a bet.

choices.label: Pick the lane: the one thing only you do.

outcome.narration: Late, but a bet is finally a bet. Now keep it.

choices.label: Hold the middle. Flexibility is the strategy.

outcome.narration: Maybe. But nobody crosses town for flexible.

title: The One-Sentence Test
text: A reviewer tried to describe {company} in one sentence and couldn't. The piece ran anyway — three qualifiers, two hedges, no verdict. Readers felt the way they already felt: unsure.

choices.label: Write the sentence yourself. Make everything match it.

outcome.narration: It costs you a launch's worth of attention. Now the sentence exists, and it's yours.

choices.label: Cut whatever doesn't fit the sentence.

outcome.narration: You kill two things you liked. What's left explains itself.

choices.label: That's the reviewer's problem.

outcome.narration: It isn't. The sentence exists now, and it reads: hard to say.

title: The Ones Who Cross Town
text: Strangers now describe {company} the way you would, word for word, unprompted. The invitation on your desk exists because of that — the kind that only goes to people who mean one thing.

choices.label: Take the stage. Say the sentence.

outcome.narration: You say it in one line and sit down. The room repeats it for you.

choices.label: Send the work instead of the founder.

outcome.narration: The work travels. You sleep.

title: Called First
text: Nobody calls {company} original. They call you first. A big-box buyer wants the operator who ships the proven thing faster than the people who proved it.

choices.label: Take the volume deal.

outcome.narration: More units, thinner slices. The machine likes being fed.

choices.label: Hold your terms. Speed is the product.

outcome.narration: You quote the same number twice, slower the second time. They sign.
